column6: The back-translated paragraph maintains the same conceptual meaning as the original, using different wording but conveying the same ideas about the topics discussed in the previous chapters.
column7: In the previous two chapters we have discussed several important topics. We explored the role and ministry of the Holy Spirit, as well as the role and ministry of the church.
column8: In the past two chapters, we have addressed several important themes. We have explored the role and work of the Holy Spirit, as well as the role and work of the Church.

column6: Both paragraphs convey the same idea that work continues after conversion due to unresolved memories, unchanged beliefs, and persistent habits, emphasizing the connection between the mind and its fleshly nature.
column7: We know there is continued work to be done after conversion because our painful memories didn’t resolve, many of our beliefs stayed the same, and many of our habits or rituals didn’t vanish. Furthermore, conversion did not separate our minds from their fleshly (carnal) nature.
column8: We see that dealings must continue even after conversion because our painful memories have not been resolved, many beliefs remain, and many habits and rituals have not disappeared. Moreover, conversion did not sever our mind from its carnal (of the flesh) nature.

column6: Both paragraphs convey the same idea about the process of growing up and the tendency to revert to self-centered thinking, with no significant changes in meaning or intent.
column7: Part of growing up is maturing past our childish ways, but when pressed we very easily resort to a pattern of thinking and living oriented around the self. As James says:
column8: Part of becoming an adult is maturing out of childish ways, but when pressed, we can very easily revert to patterns of self-centered thinking and living. As James says.

column6: Both paragraphs convey the same core message about God's desire to transform our inner selves and guide us away from worldly ways, emphasizing the understanding of His will as good, pleasing, and perfect.
column7: God wants to fundamentally transform our minds and our pattern of thinking. His desire is for us not to be conformed to the way of the world, but that we will know what is good (beneficial), pleasing (acceptable), and the perfect (complete & lacking nothing) will of God.
column8: God desires to fundamentally change our hearts and our patterns of thought. His desire is that we not assimilate to the ways of the world, but that we know what the will of God is—that is, what is good（beneficial）, pleasing（acceptable）, and perfect（complete & lacking nothing）.

column6: The original emphasizes the need for discipline in the transformation process, while the back-translation shifts the focus to the necessity of training, which may imply a different approach or understanding of the transformation requirements.
column7: The requirements for transformation are really that simple, **though it takes discipline**!
column8: The requirements for transformation really are that simple, **though training is required**!

column6: The back-translated paragraph maintains the same doctrinal meaning and intent as the original, emphasizing that victory over the flesh is achieved through God's provision and the power of His Word.
column7: Our fight against the flesh will not be won by our flesh, but rather by God’s equipping for the battle of the mind. His words (the sword of truth) are mighty to correct every imagination, haughty thought, and to bring into arrest (captivity) every thought that goes against obeying God.
column8: Our battle against the flesh cannot be won by our flesh. Rather, we win with what God provides for the battle of the mind. The Word（the sword of truth）is powerful to correct every imagination and proud thought, and to place every thought under arrest（captivity）that opposes obedience to God.

column6: The back-translated paragraph maintains the same core ideas and intent as the original, emphasizing the importance of vigilance and effort in both law enforcement and personal mental discipline.
column7: When the authorities arrest some, they place them in shackles and put them in a jail cell. If that person escapes custody, they don't turn a blind eye, they will use incredible resources and not rest until that person has been brought back under control. We too should act with such zeal in the contest for our minds!
column8: When authorities arrest someone, they put handcuffs and shackles on them and put them in jail. If that person escapes restraint, they do not turn a blind eye; they expend tremendous resources and do not rest until the person is back under control. We too should act with that kind of zeal in the contest over our thoughts!
